name: U.S. housing bubble
benchmark: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index
mainTrigger: A prolonged housing-price expansion alongside abundant mortgage credit and growth in mortgage securitization.
mainCause: Highly leveraged housing finance, weakening underwriting and a repricing of mortgage credit risk.
historicalSummary: The reference series is the monthly national Case-Shiller index. It is shown as a source-backed historical benchmark; the library does not convert it into an aggregate housing-market capitalization or infer a capital-flow total.
keyLessons: Asset-price momentum can coexist with leverage and underwriting risks that do not show up in the headline index.
Credit conditions and transmission channels matter alongside the asset-price path.

timeline.title: National index peak
timeline.detail: The not-seasonally-adjusted national index recorded 184.62 in July 2006.

timeline.title: Housing downturn
timeline.detail: The historical reference classifies the post-peak period as the bust phase.

timeline.title: Post-crisis trough period
timeline.detail: The library records the trough year only; no unsupported recovery statistic is calculated.

chart.method: Published monthly Case-Shiller observations normalized to the July 2006 reading = 100. Values are annual timeline anchors, not a reconstructed monthly series.

sources.name: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index (CSUSHPINSA)
sources.organization: S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC, distributed by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

sources.name: Index observation archive

limitations: The underlying index is monthly and copyrighted; only sparse, source-attributed anchor observations are stored here.
Largest drawdown and recovery time remain unavailable in this static version rather than being independently calculated.
